    Cuttering for words

    Interactive Quick Cutter Verification

    LC Shelflisting Principles:
    • Mac, Mc and M′ file strictly as spelled.
    • A Cutter covers the letter span up to the next listed letter.
    • Do not end a Cutter with 1 or 0.
    Cuttering for Numerals:

    For Arabic or Roman numerals in titles, use .A12–.A19 (the generator assigns .A15 at the center of the span to allow room for growth).

    NERDC Curriculum Classification Scheme — 2026 Classified Edition

    Executive Conference Brief • Abuja Presentation

    The NERDC Curriculum Classification Scheme (Classified Edition with Notation, 2026; notation adapted from Ayandokun, 2026) is the official national subject classification system for Nigerian Basic and Senior Secondary schools and Media Resource Centres.

    Unlike general international schemes (such as Dewey Decimal Classification or Library of Congress Classification) which disperse Nigerian educational curricula across alien cultural categories, this scheme organizes library materials strictly according to the NERDC National Curriculum, ensuring 100% curriculum collocation for teachers, students, and school librarians.

    Structural Outline of the Scheme

    Notation Syntax & Hierarchy

    LevelHierarchyPatternWorked Example
    1Class (Broad Field)Two digits (00–04)04 Trades, Vocation and Crafts
    2SubjectClass + two digits0407 Crop Production and Horticulture
    3ThemeSubject + point + two digits0407.15 Crop and Horticulture Mgt
    4TopicTheme + lowercase Roman numeral0407.15i Field Practices
    5SubtopicTopic + capital letter0407.15iF Crop Management Practices
    6Deeper SubtopicSubtopic + lowercase letter0407.15iFc Weeding crops

    The notation possesses fixed hierarchical width at each level, ensuring exact alphanumeric filing on library shelves and in OPAC databases.

    Institutional Acknowledgments

    Developed for national deployment by the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC), Sheda, Abuja, in collaboration with Akanu Ibiam Federal Polytechnic, Unwana. Complies with the National Policy on Education, UBEC Basic Education Guidelines, and WAEC/NECO Examination Syllabuses.
